raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#47619 sorted CUDA tests by importance: some moved from **base** (every PR) to **extra** (opt-in label), others from extra to **nightly** or **weekly**. The AMD registrations in the same files were not moved, so AMD still runs 8 of these tests on every PR and 20 on every `run-ci-amd-extra` PR. Separately, two tests are registered to suites no CI job runs, so they never run anywhere.

## Modifications

Each test now runs at the same tier on AMD as on CUDA:

- **AMD base -> AMD extra (8):** `hicache_storage_file_backend`, `hicache_variants`, `unified_radix_cache_kl_full`, `sampling_mask`, `load_snapshot_server`, `retract_decode`, `streaming_session`, `dflash`.
- **AMD extra / base -> AMD nightly (20)**, because CUDA runs them nightly or weekly (AMD has no weekly):
  - 16 one-GPU tests -> `nightly-amd-1-gpu` (`basic_perf` latency / throughput / score / embeddings, `test_torch_compile`, `test_vlm_models`, attention, quantization, and 5 LoRA tests)
  - 3 two-GPU `basic_perf` throughput tests -> new `nightly-amd-2-gpu`
  - `test_lora_gpt_oss_20b_logprob_diff` -> `nightly-amd-4-gpu`
- **Never-run tests:**
  - `test_hicache_storage_3fs_backend.py` used a CUDA suite name; it now runs in AMD extra, as on CUDA.
  - `test_fp8_fused_writer_hip.py` pointed at a non-existent AMD CPU job; its checks need no GPU, so it now runs in the CPU suite `base-a-test-cpu`.

Workflow changes:

- `nightly-test-amd.yml`: the 1-GPU nightly job grows from ~5 to ~89 min of tests, so it is split into 3 shards with an 1800 s per-file limit. New `nightly-2-gpu` job on the MI300 2-GPU runners (~35 min).
- `pr-test-amd.yml`: the stage-b 1-GPU-large job needs one shard instead of two.
- `pr-test-amd-extra.yml`: shards set to the new sizes (1-GPU small 4, with the step timeout raised from 45 to 75 min, 1-GPU large 2, 2-GPU large 2). `test_hicache_variants.py` gets its real AMD `est_time` (1500 s, was 524) so the shards balance.

Cost per run: AMD base −~2 GPU-h per PR, AMD extra −~0.7 GPU-h per labeled PR, AMD nightly +~2.8 GPU-h per ROCm image.

## Verification

- Every test registered for both CUDA and AMD is now at the same tier on both (kernel tests excluded), and every AMD PR test is in a suite some job runs.
- The 17 moved tests that were in AMD extra all passed in the last finished scheduled extra run (rocm724, run 41506219333). The fp8 writer test passed on the CPU runner (5 tests OK); the 3FS test passed on an AMD 2-GPU runner (both runs from #47179).
- Lint and PR-title checks pass on this PR.
- Not yet run: the split 1-GPU nightly job and the new `nightly-2-gpu` job. A `nightly-test-amd.yml` dispatch on this branch should confirm them before merge.

## Notes for reviewers

- The 1-GPU nightly job name now ends in ` part N`, after the closing parenthesis, so the AMD job monitor (which matches `<job> (<rocm>, <runner>)`) still groups the shards into one row.
- #47946 changes the same registration lines; it should rebase after this PR.

Validation runs on this branch (rocm10):

- Nightly, the split 1-GPU job (3 shards) plus the new `nightly-2-gpu` and `nightly-4-gpu`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651504452
- AMD Extra, all jobs: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651511260
- AMD base, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` (now 1 shard) and `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651517320
- CPU, `test_fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651523751 (passed, 5 tests OK)

Nightly and Extra run with `continue_on_error`, so per-file results will be checked in the logs once they finish.

Estimated runtime change of this PR, from the AMD `est_time` sums at the base (40a64e1) and head (616b1c6), weighted by GPUs per job:

| Tier | Suite | est before → after (min) | GPU-min |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base (every PR) | stage-b 1-GPU small | 187 → 158 | −29 |
| | stage-b 1-GPU large | 40 → 22 | −18 |
| | stage-b 2-GPU large | 58 → 24 | −68 |
| | **total** | | **−115** |
| Extra (`run-ci-amd-extra`) | extra-a 1-GPU small | 53 → 93 | +40 |
| | extra-a 1-GPU large | 111 → 50 | −61 |
| | extra-a 2-GPU large | 64 → 79 | +31 |
| | extra-b 4-GPU | 9 → 6 | −12 |
| | **total** | | **−2** |
| Nightly (per ROCm image) | nightly 1-GPU | 5 → 89 | +84 |
| | nightly 2-GPU (new) | 0 → 35 | +69 |
| | nightly 4-GPU | 8 → 11 | +12 |
| | **total** | | **+165** |

The extra total looks flat because two re-estimates add no work but show up in it: `test_hicache_variants` (524 → 1500 s, +16 GPU-min) and the 2-GPU large corrections in 616b1c6 (+23 GPU-min). From the test moves alone, extra drops by about 41 GPU-min per labeled PR.

Wall time on a base run: stage-b 1-GPU large goes from 2 shards to 1 (~22 min est, about 26 min measured on main), and stage-b 2-GPU large drops from 58 to 24 min est. These are est_time figures; actual AMD runtimes vary, as the 2-GPU large shards showed.

## Claude Code Review

This repository is configured for manual code reviews. Comment `@claude review` for a one-time review, or `@claude review always` to subscribe this PR to a review on every future push.

<sub>Tip: disable this comment in your organization's [Code Review settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code#code-review).</sub>

The tier moves match the description, and the stage-b 1-GPU-large merge into one shard fits under the timeout (about 26 min of tests, based on recent main runs).

`extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd` was close to its step timeout. In the Extra dispatch on this branch (run 41665991348), shard 0's test step took 32 min and shard 1's took 50 min, against `timeout-minutes: 60`. The shards are split on est_time, and several AMD values were far from MI300 rocm10 runtimes.

Update: pushed 616b1c6, which sets each AMD est_time in that suite to its measured runtime plus a little headroom. Re-splitting the shards on the new values gives about 37 and 39 min.

| Test | est_time | Measured | New |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hicache_storage_file_backend` | 790 | 1062 | 1100 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pp_perturb` | 298 | 500–523 | 540 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pd_perturb` | 231 | 295–435 | 450 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pp_baseline` | 243 | 294 | 320 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pd_baseline` | 106 | 162 | 180 |
| `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` | 72 | 176 | 190 |
| `test_load_snapshot_server` | 450 | 298 | 330 |
| `test_update_weights_from_distributed` | 400 | 139 | 160 |

Separately, the `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` failure in that shard looks unrelated to this PR: on main it passed right after a PD test, so it is probably flaky.

Validation runs on this branch (rocm10):

- Nightly, the split 1-GPU job (3 shards) plus the new `nightly-2-gpu` and `nightly-4-gpu`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651504452
- AMD Extra, all jobs: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651511260
- AMD base, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-large-amd` (now 1 shard) and `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651517320
- CPU, `test_fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41651523751 (passed, 5 tests OK)

Nightly and Extra run with `continue_on_error`, so per-file results will be checked in the logs once they finish.

Estimated runtime change of this PR, from the AMD `est_time` sums at the base (40a64e1) and head (616b1c6), weighted by GPUs per job:

| Tier | Suite | est before → after (min) | GPU-min |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base (every PR) | stage-b 1-GPU small | 187 → 158 | −29 |
| | stage-b 1-GPU large | 40 → 22 | −18 |
| | stage-b 2-GPU large | 58 → 24 | −68 |
| | **total** | | **−115** |
| Extra (`run-ci-amd-extra`) | extra-a 1-GPU small | 53 → 93 | +40 |
| | extra-a 1-GPU large | 111 → 50 | −61 |
| | extra-a 2-GPU large | 64 → 79 | +31 |
| | extra-b 4-GPU | 9 → 6 | −12 |
| | **total** | | **−2** |
| Nightly (per ROCm image) | nightly 1-GPU | 5 → 89 | +84 |
| | nightly 2-GPU (new) | 0 → 35 | +69 |
| | nightly 4-GPU | 8 → 11 | +12 |
| | **total** | | **+165** |

The extra total looks flat because two re-estimates add no work but show up in it: `test_hicache_variants` (524 → 1500 s, +16 GPU-min) and the 2-GPU large corrections in 616b1c6 (+23 GPU-min). From the test moves alone, extra drops by about 41 GPU-min per labeled PR.

Wall time on a base run: stage-b 1-GPU large goes from 2 shards to 1 (~22 min est, about 26 min measured on main), and stage-b 2-GPU large drops from 58 to 24 min est. These are est_time figures; actual AMD runtimes vary, as the 2-GPU large shards showed.

reviews.body:
## Claude Code Review

This repository is configured for manual code reviews. Comment `@claude review` for a one-time review, or `@claude review always` to subscribe this PR to a review on every future push.

<sub>Tip: disable this comment in your organization's [Code Review settings](https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code#code-review).</sub>

The tier moves match the description, and the stage-b 1-GPU-large merge into one shard fits under the timeout (about 26 min of tests, based on recent main runs).

`extra-a-test-2-gpu-large-amd` was close to its step timeout. In the Extra dispatch on this branch (run 41665991348), shard 0's test step took 32 min and shard 1's took 50 min, against `timeout-minutes: 60`. The shards are split on est_time, and several AMD values were far from MI300 rocm10 runtimes.

Update: pushed 616b1c6, which sets each AMD est_time in that suite to its measured runtime plus a little headroom. Re-splitting the shards on the new values gives about 37 and 39 min.

| Test | est_time | Measured | New |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hicache_storage_file_backend` | 790 | 1062 | 1100 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pp_perturb` | 298 | 500–523 | 540 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pd_perturb` | 231 | 295–435 | 450 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pp_baseline` | 243 | 294 | 320 |
| `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_pd_baseline` | 106 | 162 | 180 |
| `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` | 72 | 176 | 190 |
| `test_load_snapshot_server` | 450 | 298 | 330 |
| `test_update_weights_from_distributed` | 400 | 139 | 160 |

Separately, the `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` failure in that shard looks unrelated to this PR: on main it passed right after a PD test, so it is probably flaky.
